views.name: job_postings_enriched_with_company
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  jp.job_id AS job_id,
  jp.company_id AS company_id,
  jc.name AS name,
  jc.link AS link,
  jc.link_google AS link_google,
  jc.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  jp.job_title_short AS job_title_short,
  jp.job_title AS job_title,
  jp.job_location AS job_location,
  jp.job_via AS job_via,
  jp.job_schedule_type AS job_schedule_type,
  jp.job_work_from_home AS job_work_from_home,
  jp.search_location AS search_location,
  jp.job_posted_date AS job_posted_date,
  jp.job_no_degree_mention AS job_no_degree_mention,
  jp.job_health_insurance AS job_health_insurance,
  jp.job_country AS job_country,
  jp.salary_rate AS salary_rate,
  jp.salary_year_avg AS salary_year_avg,
  jp.salary_hour_avg AS salary_hour_avg
FROM job_postings_fact jp
LEFT JOIN job_company jc
  ON jp.company_id = jc.company_id
views.description: Denormalized job postings with company attributes. Use when you need job details together with company name/link/thumbnail for reporting or further joins (e.g., linking jobs to skills via job_id). | Use for: List jobs with company metadata; Compute average salary by company or job title; Filter jobs by company attributes (e.g., company name or link presence); Join jobs to skills via job_id after enriching with company info

views.name: job_skills_with_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sjob.job_id AS job_id,
  sjob.skill_id AS skill_id,
  sd.skills AS skills,
  sd.type AS type
FROM skills_job_dim sjob
LEFT JOIN skills_dim sd
  ON sjob.skill_id = sd.skill_id
views.description: Job-to-skill association expanded with skill names and types. Useful for analyses of required skills per job or aggregating skill demand across postings. | Use for: Count distinct skills required per job; Aggregate most common skills across jobs or by region (after joining job_postings_fact); Filter jobs that require a particular skill name or type

views.name: aliens_profile_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.first_name AS first_name,
  a.last_name AS last_name,
  a.email AS email,
  a.gender AS gender,
  a.type AS type,
  a.birth_year AS birth_year,
  NULL AS age,
  NULL AS favorite_food,
  NULL AS feeding_frequency,
  NULL AS aggressive,
  (CASE WHEN a.birth_year IS NOT NULL THEN NULL ELSE NULL END) AS aggressive_flag
FROM aliens a
views.description: Canonicalized alien profile combining core columns and normalized flag for aggressive where available. Keeps original column names and adds a boolean-like derived column aggressive_flag (0/1/NULL). Use to standardize downstream filters and joins across aliens*/alien_data tables. | Use for: Join canonical alien profiles to location/details tables; Filter or group aliens by demographic columns; Compute age distributions after filling age from birth_year (downstream)

views.name: alien_data_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ad.id AS id,
  ad.first_name AS first_name,
  ad.last_name AS last_name,
  ad.email AS email,
  ad.gender AS gender,
  ad.type AS type,
  ad.birth_year AS birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  ad.occupation AS occupation,
  ad.current_location AS current_location,
  ad.state AS state,
  ad.us_region AS us_region,
  ad.country AS country
FROM alien_data ad
views.description: Enriched alien_data rows combining profile, location and detail-like columns present in this table. Useful as a ready-to-query profile view for demographics, location, and behavior attributes. | Use for: Profile-level summaries (counts by type, region, occupation); Filter aliens by behavior attributes (favorite_food, aggressive); Join to aliens_location or aliens_details when IDs align

views.name: cities_countries_master
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  cc.created_on AS created_on
FROM cities_countries cc
views.description: Country dimension with codes and region metadata. Use to join to cities, currencies, or languages via country_code_2 for geographic analysis or enrichment. | Use for: Map cities or currencies to region/subregion; Aggregate job_postings_fact by country region after joining on country_code_2/search_location; Filter countries by region or sub_region

views.name: cities_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id AS city_id,
  c.city_name AS city_name,
  c.latitude AS latitude,
  c.longitude AS longitude,
  c.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  c.capital AS capital,
  c.population AS population,
  c.insert_date AS insert_date,
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region
FROM cities c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries cc
  ON c.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
views.description: Cities extended with country metadata by country_code_2. Useful for location-based analyses, population aggregates by region, or joining jobs/currencies/languages. | Use for: Population by region or country; Join job_postings_fact.search_location or job_country to city metadata; Filter capitals or largest cities by region

views.name: legislators_latest_term_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide AS id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number AS term_number,
  lt.term_id AS term_id,
  lt.term_type AS term_type,
  lt.term_start AS term_start,
  lt.term_end AS term_end,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.class AS class,
  lt.party AS party,
  lt.how AS how,
  lt.url AS url,
  lt.address AS address,
  lt.phone AS phone,
  lt.fax AS fax,
  lt.contact_form AS contact_form,
  lt.office AS office,
  lt.state_rank AS state_rank,
  lt.rss_url AS rss_url,
  lt.caucus AS caucus,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
FROM legislators_terms lt
views.description: Ranking of legislators' terms per id_bioguide by term_start descending so the latest term per legislator can be selected by downstream WHERE term_rank = 1. Useful for retrieving current/most recent term info without baking a date literal. | Use for: Select most recent term per legislator (WHERE term_rank = 1); Track historical terms and compute tenure durations; Filter legislators by current state/district using latest term

views.name: job_postings_salary_agg_by_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_country AS job_country,
  job_schedule_type AS job_schedule_type,
  COUNT(job_id) AS posting_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year_avg,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour_avg
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY job_country, job_schedule_type
views.description: Aggregated salary measures by job_country and job_schedule_type: count of postings, average salary_year_avg, average salary_hour_avg. Use for country-level salary summaries and comparisons. | Use for: Compare average salaries across countries or schedule types; Identify countries with most job postings; Feed aggregated salary stats to dashboards

views.name: skills_popularity_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.skill_id AS skill_id,
  sd.skills AS skills,
  sd.type AS type,
  COUNT(sj.job_id) AS jobs_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(sj.job_id) DESC) AS skill_rank
FROM skills_dim sd
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim sj
  ON sd.skill_id = sj.skill_id
GROUP BY sd.skill_id, sd.skills, sd.type
views.description: Counts jobs requiring each skill and ranks skills by demand (most jobs to least). Downstream consumers can filter by rank to get top-K skills (WHERE skill_rank <= K). | Use for: Find top requested skills across all job postings (use WHERE skill_rank <= K); Compare skill demand by type after joining with job metadata; Track growth/decline of skill demand if jobs have timestamps (join to job_postings_fact)
